long_biography.plain_text:
Before becoming a restaurateur, Jean-Jack Bertrand represented France in skiing and won national downhill titles. He initially helped at Le Tremplin at his father’s urging, then took charge of the Courchevel restaurant in 1998. Bertrand broadened its dining offer with a crêperie and introduced products encountered while travelling. The family enterprise remained central to his career until its restaurant business and associated property interests were sold to an LVMH subsidiary in 2025.

Bertrand also acquired L’Auberge de Savoie in Moûtiers, a hotel and restaurant operated through a company directed by his holding business. He remains president of that holding company, which continues to direct the hotel business. His career bridges competitive skiing and the hospitality trade in the French Alps.
